title: Gifts to a department from organizations the same department pays
question: Which organizations gave a department gifts while that department was paying them, and how much each way?
finding: 18 donor-and-department pairs where an organization gave the department gifts valued at $2.6 million in all while the same department paid it $25,000 or more in the fiscal years around the gift. Largest: San Francisco Symphony to Arts Commission (ART), $2.2 million given, $13.5 million paid. By department: Arts Commission (ART) $2.2 million; War Memorial (WAR) $247,689; Airport (AIR/SFO) $37,548; Recreation and Parks (REC) $32,800. 1,389 gifts from donors whose names read as individuals are counted and not matched.
how: Itemised gifts (list downloaded 12 November 2026) joined to the cover page for the department; organization donors matched by normalised name to the payment file for the same department code; payments summed for the fiscal year of the gift and the years before and after. A pair is listed when that sum is at least $25,000. the site’s “Side doors: department gifts, commissioners, ballot committees, enforcement” page (gifts-to-departments) counts a wider set that also uses the department's own note on the form.
limits: Many such donors are foundations, hospitals or arts groups that the department funds for services, and give back to a programme; the rules permit a gift from a payee when reported. The match is by name. Payments are department totals, not tied to any decision. The test cannot see payments made through another department or a fiscal sponsor.
